claim: Three rolling writers name the next part by incrementing, and none asks whether that name is free. Each finds its last part by walking contiguously from part 1 and stopping at the first gap, so a part past a gap is invisible to the writer that would name it next. Where the name is taken the file is opened for append rather than replaced, so live lines join the middle of what is already there. The log roller alone then zeroes its own byte count, so it would pour up to a full ceiling into a file it never measured, while the other two re-read the file's size before each append and would put at most one line in.

evidence:
Read 2026-09-12 at HEAD. Nothing was run: bun is refused inside the checkout, so this is read off the code rather than exercised.

THE ROLL. `agent/seat/log-day/modules/log-day-writing/log-day-writing.module.code.ts:261-271` reads `if (bytes > 0 && bytes + size > ENTRY_CEILING)`, then `const next = partAt(pagePath, part + 1)`, a guard on `next === null`, then `part += 1`, `path = join(root, next)`, `bytes = 0`. There is no `existsSync` on `next`. Line 278 writes with `appendFile`, so a name already taken is joined rather than replaced. `lastPartOf` at lines 136-151 walks up from `FIRST_PART` and breaks at line 146 on `!existsSync(join(root, next))`, so `part` counts the contiguous parts rather than the parts present. Those two together are what let `part + 1` be occupied and let the writer not know it.

THE SAME SHAPE TWICE MORE. `change/modules/edits-keeping/edits-keeping.module.code.ts:160-184`: `fillingAt` breaks on the same test at line 166, names `partAt(page, part + 1)` at line 173 with no existence test, and `appended` writes `appendFileSync` at line 182. `check/modules/cost/check-cost.module.code.ts:293-315`: `fillingAt` breaks at line 304, names the next part at line 313, and `appendedIn` appends at line 340. No sibling makes the check the log roller omits.

WHAT THE ROLLER ALONE DOES. Both siblings call `sizeOnDisk` on the part they found, at `edits-keeping.module.code.ts:170` and `check-cost.module.code.ts:308`, on every append, so an occupied part would be measured and rolled past after one line. The roller raises `bytes` in a closure at line 227 and sets it to 0 at line 269, so it would append up to ENTRY_CEILING, 8,388,608 bytes at `page/modules/entry-ceiling/entry-ceiling.module.code.ts:1`, on top of whatever the file already held.

WHO ELSE NAMES A PART. The roller's names carry the uncommitted mark: `uncommittedPartAt` composes `<page>.lines.partN.uncommitted.jsonl` through `page/modules/file-parts/page-file-parts.module.code.ts:20-27` and `page/modules/file-name/page-file-name.module.code.ts:180-186`. The only other caller composing that name is `change/mechanical/file/rename/rename-file-page/rename-file-page.change-mechanical.code.ts:130-136`, which renumbers a page's uncommitted parts from one by index as it carries them to the new name. `change/mechanical/file/divide/divide-file-page-property/divide-file-page-property.change-mechanical.code.ts:79-86` writes `partN` names for any page and any property, but through the committed `partsOf`, so it never names a `lines` part. So no second program contends for a log part today. What holds the roller up is an assumption it neither states nor tests.

WHAT THE DAMAGE WOULD LOOK LIKE. Nothing about the file's form would be wrong. The lines would still be JSONL, still one object to a line, out of order only against the timestamps they carry, and `partFiled` at line 279 would file the path as newly opened whether or not it was. Whether any reader of these lines judges their order was not established. The one consequence a check is written for is the overshoot: `check/code/pages/file-length/file-length.check-code.decision.code.ts:83` gives any `.jsonl` file ENTRY_CEILING, so a part carried past it would be named by size, long after the joining, and saying nothing of the order.
